title: Repeatable list flags (--reference, --label, --add-* on task edit) silently corrupt a JSON-array value into one malformed entry
description:
Reported inbound by opum-marketplace via the orchestrator (opum-agent) while creating OMARK-23: quest task create --reference '["a","b"]' stores the entire JSON-array string as ONE malformed reference and exits 0 with no error, warning, or diagnostic. opum-marketplace caught it only by diffing the created task against a known-good shape, then repaired it with three --add-reference calls plus one --remove-reference.

Why this is worse than a plain parse failure: --acceptance-criteria and --definition-of-done on the SAME command require exactly one JSON-array-string occurrence (a repeat is rejected as a usage error, parsed/validated by checkListValue), so a caller who has just learned that convention from those flags will reasonably reach for it on --reference too -- and get silent corruption instead.

Root cause, confirmed by reading the source (src/cli/main.ts): --acceptance-criteria/--definition-of-done are NOT registered in flags()'s repeatableValueFlags set, so a second occurrence throws '--x may only be provided once', and the single occurrence's value is JSON.parsed + validated by checkListValue/stringValue. In contrast, --label, --doc, --alias, --assignee, --reference, --modified-file, and --dependency on 'task create' (main.ts ~1981-1994, ~2045-2059) ARE registered as repeatable, so each occurrence pushes its RAW STRING onto an array via parsed.values.get(...) with zero JSON parsing or shape validation -- a JSON-array-string given as one occurrence becomes one literal array element, indistinguishable from a legitimate single value containing brackets.

This is not limited to --reference: the identical shape exists on 'task edit's --add-label, --add-dependency, --add-assignee, --add-reference, --add-modified-file (main.ts ~2368-2388, ~2473-2507) and their --remove-* counterparts, all read via the same unvalidated parsed.values.get(...) pattern. Any of them will silently accept and store a JSON-array-string as one corrupted entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Passing a JSON array to --reference (or --label/--doc/--alias/--assignee/--modified-file/--dependency) on task create either splits it into the intended multiple values or is rejected as a usage error -- never silently stored as one malformed entry
The same fix applies to task edit's --add-label/--add-dependency/--add-assignee/--add-reference/--add-modified-file and their --remove-* counterparts

A design decision is recorded (in the task's notes or an ADR) on which of the two established conventions on this command -- repeat-the-flag vs one-JSON-array-occurrence -- these fields adopt going forward, since accept-and-split and reject-as-usage-error are both defensible and the orchestrator left the choice to whoever implements this
Regression tests cover at least one flag from each of the two affected commands (task create and task edit) given a JSON-array-string value

implementationNotes: DESIGN DECISION (AC3): reject-loud, not accept-and-split. Confirmed via implementation rather than assumed: task create/task edit already carry a deliberate two-family convention -- --acceptance-criteria/--definition-of-done (create) and --labels/--plan/--notes (edit, full-replace) take exactly ONE JSON-array-string occurrence; --label/--doc/--alias/--assignee/--reference/--modified-file/--dependency (create) and their --add-*/--remove-* edit counterparts take ONE RAW VALUE PER OCCURRENCE, repeated for multiple values, with no JSON-array form at all. Collapsing them (accept-and-split) would erase that real distinction and silently change semantics for any existing caller whose literal value happens to start with [ and parse as JSON -- for these id/path/name fields that is vanishingly unlikely to be intended, but not impossible, so a loud, named usage error is strictly safer than guessing. Implemented as a shared rejectArrayLookingValue() helper in src/cli/main.ts: parses the value, and only rejects when it successfully parses AND is a JSON array -- so ordinary values (including ones starting with '[') pass through untouched, and only genuinely array-shaped values trip it.\n\nScope, beyond the flags named in this task's AC2: also guarded task edit's --doc (edit's raw full-replace form of documentation, same code shape as create's --doc) and --remove-comment (reads a comment id per occurrence via the same unvalidated parsed.values.get(...) pattern as --remove-label/--remove-dependency, though --add-comment/--comments already validate a JSON payload via commentsValue and were correctly left alone). Deliberately NOT applied to --add-plan/--remove-plan/--add-note/--remove-note/--append-final-summary: free-text fields where genuine content starting with '[' is materially more plausible than on an id/path/name field, and none of them has an established JSON-array sibling convention. Also found the identical raw-repeatable-flag pattern on milestone create/edit's --task/--add-task/--remove-task/--replace-task -- left out of this task's scope (task create/edit only, per how this was scoped) and worth a follow-up if judged real.
finalSummary:
Fixed. task create (--label, --doc, --alias, --assignee, --reference, --modified-file, --dependency) and task edit (--add-label/--remove-label, --doc, --add-dependency/--remove-dependency, --add-assignee/--remove-assignee, --add-reference/--remove-reference, --add-modified-file/--remove-modified-file, plus --remove-comment found sharing the identical pattern) now reject a JSON-array-shaped value with a named usage error instead of silently storing the whole array-string as one malformed entry.

Design decision (see the note above for full reasoning): reject-loud, per the orchestrator lean and confirmed correct by investigation -- these flags and --acceptance-criteria/--labels/--plan/--notes are two deliberately different, already-established conventions on the same commands, and collapsing them would silently change semantics for a rare but real edge case rather than restore consistency.

Implementation: a shared rejectArrayLookingValue(flag, values) helper in src/cli/main.ts, wired in at both task create and task edit right after their usage-argument check. It only rejects a value that successfully JSON.parses AND is an array -- an ordinary value, including one that happens to start with "[", passes through untouched.

Verified live and via a new regression test (cli-semantics.test.ts): every guarded flag rejects a JSON-array value with exit 2 and the expected message on both create and edit; a legitimate value (including one starting with "[" that is not valid JSON) still succeeds; the correct repeated-flag form still works unchanged; and the deliberately-unguarded --add-plan still accepts a value that happens to look like JSON, proving the guard is scoped, not blanket.

bun run check: typecheck/lint/format/layer:check all pass; 432 tests, 0 fail (1 pre-existing unrelated lint warning, confirmed present on dev before this branch).
